standard.title: Contribute to discussions involving diverse views
standard.description: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare experiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges using argument structures and discussion management (AC9LS10C01). They have not yet contributed systematically to multi-perspective discussions, used persuasive language for topical issues, or participated in collaborative media or broadcast contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students contribute to discussions involving diverse views — using agreement, disagreement, negotiation and persuasive language to address issues and compare experiences.

nodes.label: Expressing agreement, disagreement and encouraging participation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express agreement and disagreement, encourage others' contributions, and use turn-taking strategies in group discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: Express at least one agreement and one disagreement using target language conventions; use at least one strategy to invite another person's contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Use varied expressions for agreement and disagreement; provide encouragement and acknowledgement in discussion; take turns and manage overlapping contributions; negotiate shared decisions in collaborative contexts.
wider: Facilitate a group discussion — ensuring balanced contribution and summarising diverse views at the end
Respond to a position that conflicts with their own — using target language conventions for polite but direct disagreement
nodes.hinge_reason: Expressing agreement and disagreement through target language conventions — not only through the logic of what is said — is the social foundation for genuine multi-perspective discussion. Students who only express opinion without these conventions cannot participate in the collaborative and persuasive tasks that follow.

response_modes.reason: Agreement and disagreement conventions require a bank of expressions for varied levels of alignment and contexts. Students need varied practice across different discussion types.

success_criteria: Expresses at least one agreement and one disagreement using appropriate target language conventions
Uses at least one strategy to invite another person's contribution

nodes.label: Negotiating outcomes and reaching shared decisions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can negotiate arrangements, weigh up alternatives and reach shared decisions through target language interaction.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a negotiation that reaches a shared decision — contributing at least one alternative and responding to at least one from another participant.
nodes.typical_width: Negotiate arrangements and alternatives across varied planning and decision contexts; weigh up options using evaluative language; reach shared decisions through compromise and persuasion; participate in simulated and real transactions involving negotiation.
wider: Negotiate a genuinely contested decision with competing constraints — demonstrating that the outcome reflects real compromise
Participate in a transaction with an unexpected complication — applying negotiation strategies spontaneously to resolve it

response_modes.reason: Negotiation skills develop through varied decision contexts — different stakes, different types of alternatives, different interlocutor positions each require different negotiation strategies.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Genuine negotiation toward shared outcomes in the target language is where communication serves a real cooperative purpose — not only individual expression.
success_criteria: Contributes at least one alternative and responds to another participant's contribution in a negotiation
The negotiation reaches a shared decision or outcome through target language interaction

nodes.label: Using persuasive language for topical issues
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use argument and persuasive language to contribute to discussion of topical issues — including social, environmental and cultural topics.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two persuasive language moves in a discussion of a topical issue; acknowledge at least one opposing view.
nodes.typical_width: Use argument and persuasive language to discuss topical issues; structure contributions to introduce, support and conclude a position; acknowledge and respond to opposing views; participate in collaborative community media or broadcast projects.
wider: Contribute to a multi-perspective discussion on a topical issue where participants hold genuinely different positions — sustaining the argument through at least three exchange turns
Produce a persuasive contribution to a community media project — presenting a position on a real issue to a real audience

response_modes.reason: Using persuasive language for topical issues integrates all prior discussion capabilities — agreement/disagreement (N1), negotiation (N2) — and applies them in an argument context with genuine intellectual stakes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Discussing topical issues with genuine persuasive intent — not only rehearsing arguments — is where target language use serves real civic and intellectual purposes.
success_criteria: Uses at least two persuasive language moves in a discussion of a topical issue
Acknowledges at least one opposing view in the course of the discussion
